newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Bidvest buys up Waltons.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Bidvest buys up Waltons.

text.p: South African industrial holding firm Bidvest Group Ltd said on Tuesday it had acquired struggling stationary firm Waltons Stationary Co Ltd for a one billion rand price tag.
The deal is effective immediately. The company will pay former Waltons majority shareholder Pepkor an additional 39 million rand for a restraint of trade agreement.

The deal gives Bidvest control over the entire business of Waltons including all accompanying trademarks in return for the issue of 28 million Bidvest ordinary shares at a price of 34.50 rand a share, Bidvest said in a statement.

Pepkor said earlier on Tuesday that it had sold its holdings in Waltons Consolidated Investment Holdings Ltd and its subsidiary Waltons Stationery for 408 million rand to Investec and an institutional investor.
Investec paid 9.68 rand per share for the 15 percent Pepkor held directly in Waltons and 9.35 rand per share for the 34.9 percent held in Walhold.
Pepkor said its remaining 18.2 percent interest in Walhold was taken up by an unnamed institutional investor.

It also said that Bidvest had paid 39 million rand cash for the restraint of trade agreement prohibiting Pepkor from entering into competition with business currently undertaken by Waltons for two years.

The Waltons acquisition is the largest in Bidvest's history and entrenches the company within the top 35 companies on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange in terms of market capitalisation on a fully diluted basis.
Bidvest chairman Brian Joffe said in statement his group's core interests in trading, distribution, services and light manufacturing would add value to corresponding businesses within Waltons.
With Bidvest's operating subsidiaries being highly cash generative, the group would remain comfortably cash flush even after the Waltons acquisition, he added.
"This means that we are still aggressively on the acquisition trail and we hope to make several important moves in this direction into the relatively near future," Joffe said.
In the year to February 28, Waltons' headline earnings slumped to 50.0 cents a share from 69.4 cents before.

It said at the time that the causes of the poor performance had been identified and a planned strategy had been put in place to restructure management, rationalise operations and improve financial reporting.

Pepkor's chairman Christo Wiese said earlier on Tuesday his group had decided to sell its interest in Walhold and Waltons to focus on other expansion opportunities opening up for the group in Africa and abroad.
